findings.title: Mode C scenario still says 'the BEGIN emit, as in Mode B' — a residual ripple of the resolved mode-aware CRITICAL
findings.recommendation: The Mode C accept scenario reads '...creates explore.md (and the minimal .openspec.yaml and the BEGIN emit, as in Mode B), back-fills the Premise and Decisions sections...'. Two problems cutting against the option-A resolution: (1) 'as in Mode B' grammatically covers the BEGIN emit — a content-identity reading (zero counts + Early canonical) contradicts orbit-run-summary-emit's Mode C scenario (BACK-FILLED counts); (2) the sentence orders the emit BEFORE the back-fill, while the emit must carry the back-filled counts. The other four artifacts are unambiguous, so implementation risk is low — but this is the one normative scenario still permitting the pre-resolution reading. Reword: create explore.md → back-fill → write metadata (as in Mode B) → fire the BEGIN emit (mode-aware, back-filled counts per orbit-run-summary-emit's Mode C scenario) → continue as Mode B.

findings.title: Fault-isolation's emit-less fallback pointer aims at the wrong requirement
findings.recommendation: The fault-isolation requirement says 'next falls back per the sourcing requirement' — but the sourcing requirement defines no emit-less fallback (it asserts the begin emit guarantees one exists); the actual fallback lives in the continuity requirement's emit-less scenario. Aim the pointer at the continuity requirement's emit-less rule (or add the fallback clause to the sourcing requirement).

findings.title: Tasks 2.2/2.3 predate the --full tuple amendment and don't name the per-entry tuple or JSON entry shape
findings.recommendation: The amendment landed in the spec and in test task 5.1, but build tasks 2.2/2.3 still describe --full as bands + nesting and the top-level JSON shape only. Not carrier-less (5.1's test forces it) — but adding 'each entry carrying its full orientation tuple' to 2.2 and the workstream entry shape to 2.3 closes the seam where an implementer builds from pre-amendment task text.

findings.title: Design mislabels the external review's provenance as 'iter-2 external'
findings.recommendation: D4 (line 78) says 'external W4' in an 'iter-2' framing and D5 (line 90) says 'iter-2 external CRITICAL', but the external file self-labels iteration 1; internal iters 1-2 were the in-context and fresh passes. Relabel both to 'external iter 1' (D6's 'iter-2 CRITICAL resolution' at line 99 is correct — that WAS the internal fresh pass) so audit-trail citations stay greppable.
